{{short description|American mathematician (1901–1984)}}
'''Leonard Mascot Blumenthal''' (February 27, 1901 &ndash; August 1984) was an American mathematician.

== Career ==
Blumenthal was Jewish.<ref name=runes>{{cite book|title=The Hebrew Impact on Western Civilization|last=Runes|first=Dagobert D.|location=New York|publisher=Philosophical Library|year=1951|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SAX4CAAAQBAJ|isbn=978-1-5040-1296-6}}</ref> He received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1927 from [[Johns Hopkins University]], under the supervision of [[Frank Morley]]; his [[dissertation]] was titled ''Lagrange Resolvents in Euclidean Geometry''.<ref name="mathgenealogy"/> He taught for the majority of his professional career at the [[University of Missouri]] and was the author of ''A Modern View of Geometry''.<ref>W. H. Freeman, 1961, and Dover Publications, 1980, {{ISBN|978-0-486-63962-8}}.</ref>

He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1933 to 1936.<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/ Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref>  According to the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]], he had 18 Ph.D. students at Missouri, among them [[Leroy Milton Kelly]] and [[William Arthur Kirk]]; he is the [[academic genealogy|academic ancestor]] of over 80 mathematicians.<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{mathgenealogy|id=8199|name=Leonard Mascot Blumenthal}}.</ref>

== Legacy ==
The Leonard M. Blumenthal Distinguished Professorship in Mathematics at the University of Missouri was established in 1992 in honor of Blumenthal. This [[endowed chair]] is given on a five-year rotating basis to Missouri mathematics professors; the Blumenthal Professors at Missouri have included John Beem, Mark Ashbaugh, Alex Koldobsky, and Zhenbo Qin.<ref>[http://www.math.missouri.edu/alumni/blumenthal.html Leonard M. Blumenthal Distinguished Professorship in Mathematics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100617131059/http://www.math.missouri.edu/alumni/blumenthal.html |date=2010-06-17 }}, [[University of Missouri]] Department of Mathematics.</ref> The American Mathematical Society also issued the [[Blumenthal Award]] in his honor.
